Background Moldova is part of the EU’s European Neighborhood Policy (ENP) and in the Eastern Partnership framework, which aims at strengthening individual and regional relationships between the EU and countries in its neighborhood. Moldova is also part of the Energy Community Treaty since 2010 and has signed the Association Agreement with EU in June 2014, including the DCFTA which entered into force in 2016. As a follow-up, Moldova is required to ensure transposition of the EU acquis Communautaire, which underpins the EU energy legislation on electricity, gas, oil, renewables, energy efficiency and environment. The country has synchronized its electricity network with the ENTSO-E to connect to European electricity market. Considering the ongoing energy crisis, the energy sector is one of the top priorities for the Government and it is addressed in Government’s Plans and a number of policy documents, laws and regulations which outlined the need to undertake more actions towards a green and just energy transition of the Republic of Moldova. In accordance to the existing strategic planning documents, one of main priorities of the Government is to diversify the energy mix with more renewable energy, which is also fully in line with commitments under the EU Clean Energy for all Europeans package. Achieving this goal will require significant investment in the medium and long term, but also the country’s ability to attract and absorb the funds. The development of renewables, such as wind and solar, will also depend on improving the balancing capabilities of the Moldovan power system and its integration with neighboring countries. In this regard the EU and Moldova stressed the importance of resilience against any potential efforts by third parties to use energy as a geopolitical level. The EU has urged Moldova to ensure that the energy sector reform demonstrates full respect of the Energy Community acquis and is in line with the EU Third Energy Package. The EU side confirmed its support to the objective of Moldova for integration into the EU energy system and market, an important step being the recent synchronization of its electricity network with the Continental European Network (CEN). Recognizing the importance of a just and green energy transition in addressing the root causes of the ongoing crisis, the "Accelerating a Just Energy Transition in the Republic of Moldova" portfolio of interventions has emerged - co-designed with the Government and other representatives of the energy system to ensure its relevance and effectiveness. Through this Portfolio of interventions, the Government of Moldova will be further assisted to tackle the current energy crisis and energy poverty, and addressing prioritized systemic elements in the energy sector to cope with potential future energy crisis. The Accelerating a Just Energy Transition in Republic of Moldova has the following five key areas of intervention: Accelerate Energy Diversification and Efficiency: By supporting the modernization of infrastructure, buildings, and the grid, the Project aims to increase access to renewable energy sources, promote energy efficiency, and encourage investment in renewable energy and innovative technologies. Decarbonizing Industries and Economic Sectors: The Project seeks to drive the decarbonization of various economic sectors such as construction, transportation, agriculture, and the private sector. It aims to promote sustainable practices, share green business models, and develop vocational skills for the green energy sector to create equitable employment opportunities and support the transition to a low-carbon economy. Foster Sustainable Consumption Patterns: Through comprehensive public awareness campaigns and educational materials, the Project aims to deepen understanding of energy efficiency and renewable energy among community members, business leaders, and government agencies. It strives to promote behaviour change towards sustainable energy practices, particularly among vulnerable populations. Strengthen Inclusive Energy Governance: The Project recognizes the importance of inclusive energy governance at both the national and local levels. It aims to strengthen the capacity of relevant institutions and stakeholders to effectively govern and manage the energy sector. By promoting transparency, accountability, and participation, the Project seeks to ensure that decision-making processes related to energy transition are inclusive, empowering all segments of society, including marginalized groups. Addressing Energy Vulnerability and Promoting Resilience: One of the Project 's primary focus is to address energy vulnerability and promote resilience among households and businesses. It will provide further support to the Government in improving and implementing compensation mechanisms, including the established an on-bill compensation mechanism targeting the households by level of vulnerability. This intervention aims to provide immediate relief to energy-poor households and the private sector, while also fostering long-term energy resilience and efficiency. The Project places a strong emphasis on meeting the energy needs of vulnerable groups, prioritizing affordability, reliability, and sustainability. To this end, it will explore conceptualisation of decentralized energy solutions, off-grid options, and harness the role of energy access in conflict and disaster recovery efforts, livelihoods, and social inclusion. Implementation period: 2023-2027. review_candidates.description: Commissioning Manager – Data Centre Project Location: Middlesbrough, UK ( with regular visits to HQ based in London) Employment Type: Full-Time About The Role We are seeking an experienced Commissioning Manager to lead the commissioning programme on a major data centre project in Middlesbrough. This is a critical leadership position responsible for managing all commissioning activities from design review and construction readiness through integrated systems testing, client acceptance, and final handover to operations. You will oversee multidisciplinary commissioning teams covering mechanical, electrical, controls, life safety, and integrated systems, ensuring a safe, compliant, and successful delivery of this mission-critical facility. Key Responsibilities Commissioning Leadership & Strategy Develop and lead the overall commissioning strategy, execution plans, governance processes, and commissioning programme. Manage multidisciplinary commissioning teams, providing clear direction, priorities, and performance expectations. Act as the primary commissioning interface between project management, construction, design, QA/QC, HSE, planning, commercial teams, vendors, and the client. Chair commissioning coordination, readiness, integration, and handover meetings, ensuring actions are tracked and closed. Planning, Readiness & Programme Management Develop and maintain the integrated commissioning schedule, linking construction completion, vendor activities, energisation, testing, and handover milestones. Manage commissioning resources, including specialist vendors, personnel, temporary systems, test equipment, and permits. Lead system readiness reviews prior to energisation and testing, ensuring all documentation, inspections, permits, and access requirements are in place. Identify programme risks and constraints and implement recovery plans to maintain project milestones. Technical Governance & Quality Assurance Provide commissioning input into design reviews, technical submittals, RFIs, method statements, inspection and test plans, and commissioning procedures. Ensure testing activities comply with UK regulations, relevant British and European standards, project specifications, and manufacturer requirements. Oversee factory acceptance testing (FAT), site acceptance testing (SAT), energisation procedures, functional performance testing, and integrated systems testing (IST). Monitor and drive closure of defects, non-conformances, and punch-list items. Systems Integration & Handover Lead the Level 0–5 commissioning process across all mechanical, electrical and control systems. Manage lockout/tagout (LOTO), permit-to-work arrangements, system boundaries, and transfer of control processes. Develop and execute integrated systems testing strategies and operational scenarios. Coordinate client demonstrations, witnessing activities, operator training programmes, and phased handovers. Ensure all commissioning records, certifications, O&M manuals, as-built documentation, and handover dossiers are completed and accepted. Commercial & Stakeholder Management Support management of commissioning budgets, subcontractor costs, specialist vendors, temporary systems, and variations. Produce weekly and monthly commissioning reports covering progress, risks, resource requirements, readiness status, and key decisions. Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, contractors, consultants, and suppliers. Ensure effective use of digital commissioning and project management platforms for reporting and document control. About You Essential Qualifications & Experience Degree-qualified in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Building Services Engineering, or a related discipline. Equivalent industry experience will also be considered. Minimum 5 years' experience in a Commissioning Manager role on large-scale data centre, mission-critical, industrial, pharmaceutical, or similarly complex construction projects. Proven experience leading multidisciplinary commissioning teams and coordinating contractor and vendor activities. Strong knowledge of commissioning methodologies including Levels 0–5, energisation, functional testing, IST, handover, and operational readiness processes. Thorough understanding of UK construction regulations, health and safety requirements, and relevant British and European standards. Excellent leadership, stakeholder management, planning, and communication skills. Strong report writing and technical documentation capabilities. Full professional proficiency in English. Desirable Previous hyperscale or enterprise data centre experience. Experience delivering phased handovers within live operational environments. Authorised Person (AP), switching certification, commissioning certification, or equivalent industry accreditation. Familiarity with digital commissioning and quality management platforms. What We Offer This is a unique opportunity to play a pivotal role in delivering a major UK data centre project from construction completion through to fully operational status. You will work alongside leading industry professionals, manage complex commissioning activities, and help deliver a world-class mission-critical facility. In Return, We Offer Competitive salary and benefits package Career progression opportunities within a growing sector Exposure to large-scale, mission-critical projects Collaborative and international project environment Lunch allowance and additional employee benefits Opportunity to make a lasting impact on a flagship UK data centre development If you are an experienced Commissioning Manager looking to lead the successful delivery of a high-profile data centre project, we would welcome your application. Please Note To be considered for this role, applicants must be legally authorised to work in the UK. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship or support Skilled Worker visa applications for this position.
